programme.title: Wild West - America's Great Frontier
programme.desc: America's high country is the land of grizzly bears and giant trees, of frigid winters and scorching summers, of tough ranchers and gold rush fever. From the Rockies to the Sierra Nevada, survival demands endurance and know-how. From parasitic plants to thieving black bears, tenacious pikas and battling bison, it's in the high country that the west gets really wild.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from the grounds of Chiddingstone Castle in Kent. Antiques experts Claire Rawle and Thomas Plant unearth unique antiques and collectibles that tell fascinating stories of the past. Paul Martin visits a hop garden and hears about the thousands of Londoners who descended on the farms to pick the hops, a way of life that is now lost but not forgotten.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Harry Aikines-Aryeetey, Ania Magliano, Joe Swash and Jasmine Takhar take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: In Zurich, Michael Portillo has a brush with the absurd in the anarchic paintings and artistic haunts of the Dadaists, a group of artists who found refuge in the city during the First World War. He visits the impressive Grossmunster Church to find out about the rebellious pastor at the centre of the Swiss Reformation and studies the 500-year-old Froschauer Bible, the earliest German-language bible in the world. A new way of making chocolate is taking hold in the home of confectionery. Michael learns what it takes to be part of the Swiss Bean to Bar movement.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: After being brutally double-crossed by fellow Traitor Harry Clark, Paul Gorton is taking a second swipe at his rival - this time on the hunt to get one up in the world of antiques. The pair are reunited in the Scottish Highlands, vying to be the winner at auction. Aiding and abetting their efforts in Scotland are antiques experts Natasha Raskin Sharp and Roo Irvine, and they hit the road in a Morgan 4/4. In the shops, Harry stumbles on a very apt mug, while Paul resorts to unusual tactics in a bid to bump up his profits. But will it pay off?

programme.title: Amazing Hotels: Life Beyond the Lobby
programme.desc: Rob Rinder and Monica Galetti visit the Intercontinental Shanghai Wonderland, known as the world’s first 'earthscraper' hotel. Learning about the innovative architectural challenges that come with building a hotel into the side of a quarry, the team also help prepare dinner for the hotel’s 3,000 aquarium fish, test drones for the dazzling evening light show, serve guests at a private dinner and even help prepare for a young girl’s fourth birthday party.

programme.title: QI XL
programme.desc: Join Sandi Toksvig on a trip to the seaside with Ed Gamble, Lou Sanders, Sindhu Vee and Alan Davies.

programme.title: Paula McIntyre’s Hamely Kitchen
programme.desc: Paula meets the Parton family cook, Rachel Parton George, Dolly’s youngest sister, who cooks catfish for her. Paula also enjoys the best of southern BBQ with pitmaster Ben. She heads to a family-run rodeo to enjoy the show and the many food stalls. At her outdoor mountain kitchen, Paula cooks river trout with grilled green beans, crispy country ham and almond dressing, and grilled peaches with bourbon-smoked salt sauce on waffles.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as Morocco play Haiti in their final Group C match at Atlanta Stadium. Morocco had won just two of their 16 World Cup games prior to becoming the first African nation to reach a World Cup semi-final in 2022, losing 2-0 to France in Qatar. This is the first time they’ve qualified for three World Cups in a row. In their only previous World Cup appearance, in 1974, Haiti lost all three group games and conceded 14 goals. The 52-year gap between Haiti’s first and second appearance at the World Cup is the fourth longest in the tournament’s history. Group C also contains Scotland, who are facing Brazil at the same time as this game.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: As the second week of Springwatch draws to a close, Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan continue to uncover the remarkable wildlife stories unfolding at Crom, the beautiful reserve cared for by the National Trust. A mammal medley takes centre stage, with appearances from the pine marten, red squirrel and badger, whilst many of the chicks being monitored on the live cameras are beginning to fledge. Meanwhile, Iolo Williams wraps up his London adventure in Ealing, where local communities and conservation groups are working hard to restore wildlife and bring nature back into the urban landscape.

programme.title: In Ten Pictures
programme.desc: How did Vladimir Putin emerge from a shadowy existence as a KGB agent in 1980s East Germany to become one of the most powerful men on the planet? This film examines Putin’s rise to power through his enduring relationship with images, and his innate understanding of their power.

programme.title: Emma Barnett: Fighting Endometriosis
programme.desc: Emma Barnett shares her life-long struggle with endometriosis – a disease affecting one in ten women of reproductive age, which causes excruciating, often debilitating, pain. Inside Emma’s body, rogue cells similar to the lining of the womb mysteriously appear on other organs, creating lesions which bleed, scar and cause inflammation. There is no cure. Endometriosis is as common as diabetes but receives a fraction of the research funding. Emma travels across the UK to meet a few of the millions of women who, like her, are suffering. Through candid conversations, they reveal the extent to which endometriosis is devastating the lives of women – affecting fertility, work and loved ones.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Briony May Williams travels to scenic Devon and Cornwall, helping Andrew and Will swap their busy Oxfordshire town life for something with a little more sea air and a lot less stress. With every property offering its own tempting slice of country living and some serious wow factor, choosing won’t be easy. Taking a break from the house hunting, Briony meets a south Devon escapee who bought a crumbling old farmhouse on a whim five years ago and who is still lovingly bringing it back to life today.

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: A runaway rider sparks a hunt through narrow backstreets, coastguards remove hazards drifting off Bermuda’s shores, and rookie officers respond to a rush-hour crash.

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Off the west coast of Kyushu lies the Amakusa archipelago, formed of around 12 islands. Michael first takes a bullet train to the coast and then a ferry to the islands, where he is greeted by a group of island women performing the colourful, traditional haiya dance originally sung to fishermen. Michael also travels to Sakitsu, a tranquil town where Portuguese missionaries brought Christianity to Japan in the 16th century. After the religion was banned during the Edo period, worshippers hid from the authorities and became known as 'hidden Christians'. Returning to the mainland of Kyushu, Michael takes a regional train up to Kumamoto, where he encounters one of Japan’s most beloved mascots and dives into the story of one of the country's most revered historical figures, Saigo Takamori. Finally, in Shin Omuta, Michael meets Mr Matsunaga, a master swordsmith whose craft hasn’t changed for centuries.

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his railway tour through Uzbekistan on Tashkent’s suburban electric railway to one of the most spectacular and secretive pieces of Soviet Cold War engineering. Hidden high in the mountains, Michael discovers an installation straight out of a Bond movie - a solar furnace that concentrates the sun’s rays into a beam so hot it cuts through steel. From Tashkent, he picks up the high-speed train west to Samarkand and discovers how China’s Belt and Road Initiative is re-establishing old Silk Road routes with new railway connections. Arriving in the legendary ancient city fulfils a lifelong ambition for Michael. He is overwhelmed by the magnificent architecture of the Registan and moved by traditional music played at its heart. Finally, at one of Central Asia’s most important archaeological sites, Afrosiyob, 7th-century Sogdian wall paintings reveal the diverse and cosmopolitan history of this former Silk Road capital.

Taking a break from the house hunting, Briony meets a south Devon escapee who bought a crumbling old farmhouse on a whim five years ago and who is still lovingly bringing it back to life today.

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: A runaway rider sparks a hunt through narrow backstreets, coastguards remove hazards drifting off Bermuda’s shores, and rookie officers respond to a rush-hour crash.

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Off the west coast of Kyushu lies the Amakusa archipelago, formed of around 12 islands. Michael first takes a bullet train to the coast and then a ferry to the islands, where he is greeted by a group of island women performing the colourful, traditional haiya dance originally sung to fishermen. Michael also travels to Sakitsu, a tranquil town where Portuguese missionaries brought Christianity to Japan in the 16th century. After the religion was banned during the Edo period, worshippers hid from the authorities and became known as 'hidden Christians'. Returning to the mainland of Kyushu, Michael takes a regional train up to Kumamoto, where he encounters one of Japan’s most beloved mascots and dives into the story of one of the country's most revered historical figures, Saigo Takamori. Finally, in Shin Omuta, Michael meets Mr Matsunaga, a master swordsmith whose craft hasn’t changed for centuries.

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his railway tour through Uzbekistan on Tashkent’s suburban electric railway to one of the most spectacular and secretive pieces of Soviet Cold War engineering. Hidden high in the mountains, Michael discovers an installation straight out of a Bond movie - a solar furnace that concentrates the sun’s rays into a beam so hot it cuts through steel. From Tashkent, he picks up the high-speed train west to Samarkand and discovers how China’s Belt and Road Initiative is re-establishing old Silk Road routes with new railway connections. Arriving in the legendary ancient city fulfils a lifelong ambition for Michael. He is overwhelmed by the magnificent architecture of the Registan and moved by traditional music played at its heart. Finally, at one of Central Asia’s most important archaeological sites, Afrosiyob, 7th-century Sogdian wall paintings reveal the diverse and cosmopolitan history of this former Silk Road capital.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The quiz show where players must avoid Impossible answers to stay in the competition. 21 people start today’s show but how many of them will survive to face the £10,000 question?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Four more contenders face the black chair under the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. Clive Myrie hosts and asks the questions on the contestants' specialist subjects, which are the Empress Matilda, Stevie Nicks, the What Katy Did novels and Universal’s Frankenstein films of the 1930s and 40s.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Chris and Meg's Wild Summer
programme.desc: Chris Packham and stepdaughter Megan McCubbin continue their wildlife-watching road trip round Britain, this time exploring the Lake District. Megan surprises Chris with some animals that are renowned for helping to reduce stress – alpacas. They take two, named Ziggy and Danny, for a short walk and a paddle in Derwentwater. Next, they head off in search of the much more elusive red squirrel, as the Lake District is one of their last strongholds in England. They round off their first day by settling in for a pint at the Badger Bar and awaiting the arrival of its main attraction- a live badger cam. The next morning, the pair head South to Foulshaw Moss, a nature reserve for one of Britain’s rarest habitats – raised peat bog. With the help of a local wildlife enthusiast, they find the white-tailed darter, a rare dragonfly that Chris has only seen once before so he’s delighted to spot it. Continuing south to the coast, Chris takes Megs to one of his favourite places, Walney Island, where they catch sight of grey seals, eider ducks and terns. They reflect on why spending time in nature is not only therapeutic but necessary for their wellbeing.

programme.title: Britain and the Sea
programme.desc: David Dimbleby continues his voyage round Britain, sailing his boat Rocket along the south east coast from Hampshire to Kent. This was the front line coast, the edge of Britain essential to its defence and the first point of attack for invasion forces. From the great battleships of Nelson to the sea forts of Henry VIII, this is a story that embraces Britain's darkest and most heroic moments.

programme.title: Wild West - America's Great Frontier
programme.desc: America's high country is the land of grizzly bears and giant trees, of frigid winters and scorching summers, of tough ranchers and gold rush fever. From the Rockies to the Sierra Nevada, survival demands endurance and know-how. From parasitic plants to thieving black bears, tenacious pikas and battling bison, it's in the high country that the west gets really wild.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from the grounds of Chiddingstone Castle in Kent. Antiques experts Claire Rawle and Thomas Plant unearth unique antiques and collectibles that tell fascinating stories of the past. Paul Martin visits a hop garden and hears about the thousands of Londoners who descended on the farms to pick the hops, a way of life that is now lost but not forgotten.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Harry Aikines-Aryeetey, Ania Magliano, Joe Swash and Jasmine Takhar take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: In Zurich, Michael Portillo has a brush with the absurd in the anarchic paintings and artistic haunts of the Dadaists, a group of artists who found refuge in the city during the First World War. He visits the impressive Grossmunster Church to find out about the rebellious pastor at the centre of the Swiss Reformation and studies the 500-year-old Froschauer Bible, the earliest German-language bible in the world. A new way of making chocolate is taking hold in the home of confectionery. Michael learns what it takes to be part of the Swiss Bean to Bar movement.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: After being brutally double-crossed by fellow Traitor Harry Clark, Paul Gorton is taking a second swipe at his rival - this time on the hunt to get one up in the world of antiques. The pair are reunited in the Scottish Highlands, vying to be the winner at auction. Aiding and abetting their efforts in Scotland are antiques experts Natasha Raskin Sharp and Roo Irvine, and they hit the road in a Morgan 4/4. In the shops, Harry stumbles on a very apt mug, while Paul resorts to unusual tactics in a bid to bump up his profits. But will it pay off?

programme.title: Amazing Hotels: Life Beyond the Lobby
programme.desc: Rob Rinder and Monica Galetti visit the Intercontinental Shanghai Wonderland, known as the world’s first 'earthscraper' hotel. Learning about the innovative architectural challenges that come with building a hotel into the side of a quarry, the team also help prepare dinner for the hotel’s 3,000 aquarium fish, test drones for the dazzling evening light show, serve guests at a private dinner and even help prepare for a young girl’s fourth birthday party.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as Morocco play Haiti in their final Group C match at Atlanta Stadium. Morocco had won just two of their 16 World Cup games prior to becoming the first African nation to reach a World Cup semi-final in 2022, losing 2-0 to France in Qatar. This is the first time they’ve qualified for three World Cups in a row. In their only previous World Cup appearance, in 1974, Haiti lost all three group games and conceded 14 goals. The 52-year gap between Haiti’s first and second appearance at the World Cup is the fourth longest in the tournament’s history. Group C also contains Scotland, who are facing Brazil at the same time as this game.

They take all sorts of transport to catch Rhodri, and he is always one step ahead. Until finally, they’re on a raft across the sea and land right by Rhodri’s front door. Is he delighted to get his old hat back? Very. What a journey!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey is excited to get her own room. But when bedtime comes, she misses her sister Bingo.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Mum bans the girls from saying 'dunny', so they try and trick her into saying it instead.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: The Go Jetters are adventure-seeking explorers who soar around the planet fixing environmental problems caused by Grandmaster Glitch!

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: Peter is left to babysit Cotton-tail but can't resist an exciting event at the squirrel camp. He brings his sleeping sister along but soon must rescue her when she wakes up and crawls away.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. While rescuing river creatures after a storm, the Octonauts find a strange egg and come under attack by stinging platypuses.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Meet the artist known as Seventeen, who likes to paint 17 of everything. Learn all about the number 17 with Numberblock Seventeen!

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. N, O, T and E make music - and S makes more and more of it!

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Nervous about public speaking, Looph builds a robot to deliver a science talk in her place, but her friends are determined to help her do it herself.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Bella and Lift have fun blowing and popping bubbles. In the Cloud Kitchen, all the bubbles give Patch an idea for a tasty treat - blast off melon rockets!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing finds his old baby shoes. They are much too small for Bing now, but Coco loves them and so does baby Charlie. When they fit Charlie, Bing has a hard time letting them go to a new home until Charlie's first steps help Bing to realise they will be more use to someone whose feet are the right size.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘robot’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. We see a red robot, a smiling robot, a building robot, a sleeping robot and a helping robot. Dee meets a bleeping robot and has a boogie with a group of dancing robots! The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Lu upsets the other bugs when she refuses to share the most fun role in a game.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri and Lou have a big fight but find it’s too hard not to be friends.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: Ziff, Pipp and Button become painters using honey, colourful petals and an old pizza box.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos watch a chef build a tower of profiteroles in a bakery kitchen. When he leaves, they decide to build a tower of their own, getting carried away and making it taller and taller! Back in the boat, the Twirlywoos are having tea. Chickedy and Chick pump up the Fruit Tea Machine, but when they go to fetch the teapot, the machine grows taller. When they get back, they find they can't reach the button! Toodloo comes to help lift them up, but the Fruit Tea Machine grows taller still. It's only when they all stack up, one on top of the other, that the Twirlywoos can reach the button and fill the teapot.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Today, Justin and his friend go to the library and finish their day with a treat in the library cafe. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble uses his imagination by playing 'library' with the toys.

programme.title: My Petsaurus
programme.desc: Chloe and her mum are heading out for a swim at the pool. Topsy has other ideas, however.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: In Teletubbyland Dipsy is King. Tinky Winky delivers Tubby Custard and Tubby Toast to King Dipsy - whatever he wants!

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome babies Lola, Sullivan, Pip, Theo, Oakley and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their little ones at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Nigel has got a fluffy pom-pom inside his bag. All the parents and babies have different toys or objects that feel fluffy too, which are explored through play, songs and a story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to hide a safe, baby appropriate fluffy toy or object inside a fabric bag or pillowcase, to explore with their baby. Some viewers at home show what fluffy items they’ve been playing with too. The traditional nursery rhyme Mary Had a Little Lamb features, as does a story about Baby Bear exploring different textures. Plus, the Baby Bear Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with sensory bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children decorate wooden eggs, learn British Sign Language signs for chimney, horses and men, then sing and sign the nursery rhyme Humpty Dumpty Sat on a Wall.

programme.title: What’s in Your Plant Pot?
programme.desc: Heritage seed expert Lucy and the Fact Pack explore the colourful world of heritage tomatoes and discover why eating different-coloured fruits and vegetables is good for us.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: Baby rhino Malaika tries something new to eat. Hamza spots some huge hippos in the wild and helps the baby zebras at the orphanage stay cosy with some warm blankets.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: A baby Pea-Rex gets hiccups, so Ginger tries various cures to stop them.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and Bingo squabble over their magic xylophone, which has the power to freeze Dad in space and time. Dad seizes control and freezes Bluey, leaving Bingo as her only hope.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Join Duggee, a big, lovable dog, as he runs the Squirrel Club, where children can earn badges for learning new skills. Warm-hearted preschool series about trying new things.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Red and Blue compete to colour a castle and meet new arrival Purple. Discover what happens when you mix red and blue.

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Amiah-Rae finds out all about some of the smallest underwater creatures – seahorses! Chantelle meets seahorse fans Joss and Gabriel and puts on her wetsuit for an underwater safari. Rory and his son Sandy are at an aquarium just in time for seahorse feeding time. Chantelle and Rory’s fact files explain how seahorses hide, how they use their prehensile tails and how many babies they have. It’s also time to find out how seahorses help the ocean – in the food web and as an indicator species. This episode’s Teeny Tiny Task is to make some seahorse art with recycled beach materials.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Today we join sisters Eden and Ava as they become superheroes! First they create their characters ‘Nature Bunny Girl’ and ‘H-Winter Girl’ – not forgetting new personas for Mum and Dad too! After boosting their superpowers with a super-healthy smoothie, the family of heroes head to the park to try out their skills! It’s not long before they have their first mission: to rescue a toy that’s become lost in the woods. But will the heroes find the toy and save the day?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Naima's family are from Algeria. Naima is cooking a special Algerian borek for her friends to try. Borek is made from pastry, mashed potato, meat, cheese and olives. The great thing about borek is that you can add lots of different ingredients depending on what you like, and that's exactly what Naima is doing today. Naima mashes her potatoes, cuts some spring onions and sprinkles in some cinnamon before she gets the table ready for her Algerian feast. Naima's friends are not sure about the taste of cinnamon when they try it first, but will they like it cooked in her recipe? Let's hope so!

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Today, Maddie is having a fun day out. She uses a special thermal camera at an ice rink to find out how runny water freezes to make solid ice we can skate on. Next, Maddie heads to a bouncy castle factory to see how a bouncy castle is made from lots of different coloured pieces of material sewn together. She then has a go at bouncing when the finished jungle-themed bouncy castle is inflated and brought to life.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Kika is a golden Labrador and a guide dog for her owner, Dr Amit, who is blind, which means he cannot see. She is trained to use her supersight to help Dr Amit do as many things as he can by himself. Together, they make the best team! Dr Amit and Kika have an important mission to pick up a surprise cake and some party hats from the supermarket for Aunty Nina’s birthday. Kika has lots of friends at the supermarket. But first, she must use her supersight - and the help of her tiny friends, the road cones - to guide Dr Amit past the roadworks and keep him safely on the pavement. Then she has to help Dr Amit pick up the cake from the supermarket bakery and find the party hats. But the party hats have been moved! Kika must use all her powers to find them. Just wait until the rest of Dog Squad hear about this!

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet some honeybees. There can be 50,000 honeybees in one hive, and they can beat their wings 230 times per second. Honeybees do a 'waggle dance' that helps other bees find plants full of nectar. Nectar is a sugar-rich liquid, and the bees use it to make their honey. Next, they meet some naked mole rats. These incredible looking creatures live underground, and the team have to use special night vision cameras to see them. The mole rats have huge teeth, no hair and spend much of their time walking backwards. These two animals are very different, but Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the unusual and extraordinary wild connection is between them.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: The Brooklyn-Bells spend their first night together as a new family, only to be kept awake by Waffle, whose constant barking upsets Mrs Hobbs, their cat-obsessed neighbour.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona tries to keep Baba clean on a muddy spring day.

programme.title: Small Potatoes
programme.desc: Animated series about a group of potatoes who sing songs in different genres. Chip sings a heartfelt song about being a potato. Though he can't do many physical things, he is proud of who he is.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: When Yukee is asked to carry several messages across the garden to Sonny, she comes up with a clever rhyming song to help her remember them all.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs are helping Dad in the garden. When he asks them to fill the watering can, they get distracted by the strange echoes inside and are magically transported into the belly of a whale. Can they help their new friend Harriot find her singing voice?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are excited to attend the cinema together for the first time with Duggee, who teaches them that you should adhere to three rules in order for everyone to enjoy the experience: stay quiet, don’t fidget or kick the chair in front and go to the toilet before the film starts. The Squirrels quickly learn that the short films they are enjoying are only trailers before the film starts. Hopefully, the Squirrels can maintain their focus in order to watch the film all the way through to the end credits and earn their cinema badges.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: When there's nothing there to count and none is the amount, nobody does it better than Zero. Learn all about the number zero with Numberblocks Zero.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. P, E and N take on a pesky pen, who can draw anything it wants to escape them. Is the pen mightier than the word, or can they outplay it at its own game? This episode introduces the letter E and the words pen, peg and pet.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Maddie meets Tilly at the clinic, where they play in the waiting room and have a check up with the doctor. Mr Tumble is playing doctor and gives the toys a check-up, too. There's a guessing game in the spotty surprise. Featuring the signs for waiting room, doctor and bandage.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po drive to the Hidey Hup in the Tubby Car. They enjoy going on the Tubby Bouncy, the Tubby Uppy Downy, the Tubby Spinny and the Tubby Slidey.

programme.title: Andy's Dinosaur Adventures
programme.desc: Andy travels back 106 million years to the time of muttaburrasaurus, a nine-metre-long dinosaur that lived in Australia. His mission is to collect some red berries from a tree that the muttaburrasaurs like to eat. They have funny bumps on the end of their noses which make spectacular noises - really useful to scare off a hungry allosaurus that comes their way! But will Andy succeed and make it back to the museum in time?

programme.title: Molly and Mack
programme.desc: Molly examines her shelf of special things at the back of Mack’s Stall. She chooses the joke squirty flower and remembers the day she got it. When Molly and Mack take a delivery of a big box of practical jokes, Alice reveals she loves playing practical jokes on people. Alice decides to play a prank on James, which the kids at Kids Club think is hilarious, especially Magnus. Soon, James is plotting his revenge and gets his own back on Alice. Before long, there’s a ‘prank-off’ underway. As the jokes continue, Magnus gets caught up in the excitement. But, when he decides to play his own prank, he accidentally takes it too far and upsets Suki. James and Alice feel bad that they let things get out of hand, and Magnus needs to find a way to make it up to his friend.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: CBeebies’ very own motorcycle rider, Grace, show off three amazing machines that are all made to build and maintain roads! Grace helps paint new road markings in a road painter and shows off an amazing road screeding machine. Finally, she helps mend some broken road in a potholer!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Henry and his family get super soggy when they play with a water sprinkler!

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: While cleaning up a fire, the Octonauts encounter some fast-learning orangutans.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Flopsy and Mopsy borrow Peter's journal, Peter has to save them from Old Brown - but will he lose his precious journal in the process?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Happy notices a tiny fruit fly on his apple, and the Squirrels are amazed by how small it is. The fly tells them that there are things even smaller than him, and so Duggee teaches them that some things are so small that you can’t even see them – atoms. Combined, these make molecules, which in turn join to make cells, the fabric that makes up every living thing. The Squirrels discover that things can be wide, long, thin or small, and that these attributes make up all sorts of different sizes. To help understand this, they assign a line-up all the way from a small piece of dust to a huge rocket ship.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Juno gets sticky from tree sap, so Vida needs to give her a bubble bath - but she’s nervous!

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Evil Pea takes all the toys in the supermarket for herself and the Cobs to play with. Supertato climbs a big wall of boxes to try and get the toys back.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The Ducklings are determined to touch a shooting star and steal Weasy's model rocket to fly into the night sky. Weasy leaps into action to stop them.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: A rockslide blocks Ted the bus and his passengers in a mountain pass. Mojo’s mighty dozer top will make short work of those rocks... if Mojo and Bo can work together!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey is excited to get her own room. But when bedtime comes, she misses her sister Bingo.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Mum bans the girls from saying 'dunny', so they try and trick her into saying it instead.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Gadabout and Pearl need Zog's help to catch a stink beetle for an urgent cure. Little do they know, Zog has become a taxi for the gnomes.

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: Elvis has forgotten his trainers and has to wear a pair with laces, but he can’t tie them without his gran’s help. He needs to quickly learn to tie them himself if he wants to get a PB.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi, Ruby and Finn struggle to score in basketball, so Rafi wishes for a magic ball. At first, it’s fun, as every shot goes in - even trick throws. But the constant winning becomes boring, and the ball bounces endlessly into the hoop by itself. The trio try to contain it, but it escapes again and again. Finally, they return to playing with the ordinary ball, and Finn sinks a real shot, proving true victory is earned.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: After playing with her toy dinosaurs in Gran Gran's garden, JoJo decides she would love to see a real-life dinosaur! Gran Gran takes her to the museum to see the fossilised skeleton of a Tyrannosaurus rex, explaining that dinosaurs lived a very long time ago! However, it's more difficult to find the T. rex than she imagined, despite it's size. JoJo and Gran Gran get lost through time as they explore the large museum, and it's only when Ezra the tour guide gives them guidance that JoJo and Gran Gran find the amazing artefact!

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. A search for shade on a hot day leads Sarah and Duck to discover a fascinating tower in the park.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Small has invited the Iron Chicken to a picnic. But the Iron Chicken is late, and when Small looks through his telescope, he can see why. The Iron Chicken is trapped by a load of junk metal which has got caught in orbit around her nest. Major comes up with a clever solution to free the nest of the orbiting metal, but in doing so it seems he may have inadvertently lost the Iron Chicken.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa show Gramma Leeba a photo of themselves and match the pose. On the way to the Play Tree, they spot shapes in the clouds. They choose a picture book to play with and match the shapes to each other and all their friends. The game is easy for MeMo, but BaBa needs a little more help. MeMo kindly helps BaBa to play the game until it’s time for BeddyByes.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: The Tombliboos are riding in the Pinky Ponk, enjoying their Pinky Ponk iuice. Each of them makes a different funny noise when they sip their juice. Despite a request from the narrator to drink their Pinky Ponk juice gently and quietly, the game continues until everyone in the garden can hear the funny noise coming from the Pinky Ponk.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Everybody's welcome to join Ewan McGregor for a Bedtime Story about a caring little mouse, who dreams of building a safe and happy home, where everyone feels that they belong.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s the magical Pineapple attempting to perform a very difficult magic trick with the help of Kiwi.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing is a young and lovable bunny learning about the big world around him, with the help of his friends. A warm and gentle animation, based on the bestselling books by Ted Dewan.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Laa-Laa and Po have fun, first rolling a ball down a hill and then rolling each other! The Teletubbies enjoy watching children have fun rolling slowly down slopes too.

programme.title: Tee and Mo
programme.desc: Explore the amazing world around us with baby monkey Tee and his Mum, Mo. Sing along, join in with stories and get ready for some family fun!

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Yellow is happy to bring his colour to Colourland. Learn about the colour yellow with the Colourblocks.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: While looking for things to sell in their shop, Bing and Sula find their old friend Mr Rainybow - but his head is completely gone! So they decide to sell him, and after a nice lady buys his stacky bit for her toilet rolls, they look for some more things to sell. But then they find Mr Rainybow's head and are sad that they can't get the rest of him back. However, Charlie loves to knock down Mr Rainybow's rings!

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Preston needs to knock down his shed, and Mojo has the wrecking ball to do it. But first, Mojo and Bo have to get it all the way across town, which is harder than it sounds!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Introducing you to Squirrel Club are Happy’s Mum and Norrie’s Dad. There is a lot to see, starting with Duggee walking by... in two halves! Next is an instalment of the Squirrels' favourite comic book, Detective Puppy, then it's time to find out what the Rabbits think is cool and not cool. There are plenty of questions asked during this visit, and the Squirrels need to help Delivery Chipmunk with a ginormous parcel.

programme.desc: When Duggee’s old friend Rhodri goes home after a visit, he forgets his favourite hat. No worries, the Squirrels can run after him and give it back. Is he delighted to get his old hat back? Very. What a journey!

First they create their characters ‘Nature Bunny Girl’ and ‘H-Winter Girl’ – not forgetting new personas for Mum and Dad too! After boosting their superpowers with a super-healthy smoothie, the family of heroes head to the park to try out their skills! It’s not long before they have their first mission: to rescue a toy that’s become lost in the woods. But will the heroes find the toy and save the day?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Naima's family are from Algeria. Naima is cooking a special Algerian borek for her friends to try. Borek is made from pastry, mashed potato, meat, cheese and olives. The great thing about borek is that you can add lots of different ingredients depending on what you like, and that's exactly what Naima is doing today. Naima mashes her potatoes, cuts some spring onions and sprinkles in some cinnamon before she gets the table ready for her Algerian feast. Naima's friends are not sure about the taste of cinnamon when they try it first, but will they like it cooked in her recipe? Let's hope so!

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Today, Maddie is having a fun day out. She uses a special thermal camera at an ice rink to find out how runny water freezes to make solid ice we can skate on. Next, Maddie heads to a bouncy castle factory to see how a bouncy castle is made from lots of different coloured pieces of material sewn together. She then has a go at bouncing when the finished jungle-themed bouncy castle is inflated and brought to life.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Kika is a golden Labrador and a guide dog for her owner, Dr Amit, who is blind, which means he cannot see. She is trained to use her supersight to help Dr Amit do as many things as he can by himself. Together, they make the best team! Dr Amit and Kika have an important mission to pick up a surprise cake and some party hats from the supermarket for Aunty Nina’s birthday. Kika has lots of friends at the supermarket. But first, she must use her supersight - and the help of her tiny friends, the road cones - to guide Dr Amit past the roadworks and keep him safely on the pavement. Then she has to help Dr Amit pick up the cake from the supermarket bakery and find the party hats. But the party hats have been moved! Kika must use all her powers to find them. Just wait until the rest of Dog Squad hear about this!

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet some honeybees. There can be 50,000 honeybees in one hive, and they can beat their wings 230 times per second. Honeybees do a 'waggle dance' that helps other bees find plants full of nectar. Nectar is a sugar-rich liquid, and the bees use it to make their honey. Next, they meet some naked mole rats. These incredible looking creatures live underground, and the team have to use special night vision cameras to see them. The mole rats have huge teeth, no hair and spend much of their time walking backwards. These two animals are very different, but Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the unusual and extraordinary wild connection is between them.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: The Brooklyn-Bells spend their first night together as a new family, only to be kept awake by Waffle, whose constant barking upsets Mrs Hobbs, their cat-obsessed neighbour.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona tries to keep Baba clean on a muddy spring day.

programme.title: Small Potatoes
programme.desc: Animated series about a group of potatoes who sing songs in different genres. Chip sings a heartfelt song about being a potato. Though he can't do many physical things, he is proud of who he is.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: When Yukee is asked to carry several messages across the garden to Sonny, she comes up with a clever rhyming song to help her remember them all.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs are helping Dad in the garden. When he asks them to fill the watering can, they get distracted by the strange echoes inside and are magically transported into the belly of a whale. Can they help their new friend Harriot find her singing voice?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are excited to attend the cinema together for the first time with Duggee, who teaches them that you should adhere to three rules in order for everyone to enjoy the experience: stay quiet, don’t fidget or kick the chair in front and go to the toilet before the film starts. The Squirrels quickly learn that the short films they are enjoying are only trailers before the film starts. Hopefully, the Squirrels can maintain their focus in order to watch the film all the way through to the end credits and earn their cinema badges.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: When there's nothing there to count and none is the amount, nobody does it better than Zero. Learn all about the number zero with Numberblocks Zero.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. P, E and N take on a pesky pen, who can draw anything it wants to escape them. Is the pen mightier than the word, or can they outplay it at its own game? This episode introduces the letter E and the words pen, peg and pet.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Maddie meets Tilly at the clinic, where they play in the waiting room and have a check up with the doctor. Mr Tumble is playing doctor and gives the toys a check-up, too. There's a guessing game in the spotty surprise. Featuring the signs for waiting room, doctor and bandage.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po drive to the Hidey Hup in the Tubby Car. They enjoy going on the Tubby Bouncy, the Tubby Uppy Downy, the Tubby Spinny and the Tubby Slidey.

programme.title: Andy's Dinosaur Adventures
programme.desc: Andy travels back 106 million years to the time of muttaburrasaurus, a nine-metre-long dinosaur that lived in Australia. His mission is to collect some red berries from a tree that the muttaburrasaurs like to eat. They have funny bumps on the end of their noses which make spectacular noises - really useful to scare off a hungry allosaurus that comes their way! But will Andy succeed and make it back to the museum in time?

programme.title: Molly and Mack
programme.desc: Molly examines her shelf of special things at the back of Mack’s Stall. She chooses the joke squirty flower and remembers the day she got it. When Molly and Mack take a delivery of a big box of practical jokes, Alice reveals she loves playing practical jokes on people. Alice decides to play a prank on James, which the kids at Kids Club think is hilarious, especially Magnus. Soon, James is plotting his revenge and gets his own back on Alice. Before long, there’s a ‘prank-off’ underway. As the jokes continue, Magnus gets caught up in the excitement. But, when he decides to play his own prank, he accidentally takes it too far and upsets Suki. James and Alice feel bad that they let things get out of hand, and Magnus needs to find a way to make it up to his friend.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: CBeebies’ very own motorcycle rider, Grace, show off three amazing machines that are all made to build and maintain roads! Grace helps paint new road markings in a road painter and shows off an amazing road screeding machine. Finally, she helps mend some broken road in a potholer!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Henry and his family get super soggy when they play with a water sprinkler!

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: While cleaning up a fire, the Octonauts encounter some fast-learning orangutans.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Flopsy and Mopsy borrow Peter's journal, Peter has to save them from Old Brown - but will he lose his precious journal in the process?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Happy notices a tiny fruit fly on his apple, and the Squirrels are amazed by how small it is. The fly tells them that there are things even smaller than him, and so Duggee teaches them that some things are so small that you can’t even see them – atoms. Combined, these make molecules, which in turn join to make cells, the fabric that makes up every living thing. The Squirrels discover that things can be wide, long, thin or small, and that these attributes make up all sorts of different sizes. To help understand this, they assign a line-up all the way from a small piece of dust to a huge rocket ship.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Juno gets sticky from tree sap, so Vida needs to give her a bubble bath - but she’s nervous!

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Evil Pea takes all the toys in the supermarket for herself and the Cobs to play with. Supertato climbs a big wall of boxes to try and get the toys back.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The Ducklings are determined to touch a shooting star and steal Weasy's model rocket to fly into the night sky. Weasy leaps into action to stop them.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: A rockslide blocks Ted the bus and his passengers in a mountain pass. Mojo’s mighty dozer top will make short work of those rocks... if Mojo and Bo can work together!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey is excited to get her own room. But when bedtime comes, she misses her sister Bingo.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Mum bans the girls from saying 'dunny', so they try and trick her into saying it instead.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Gadabout and Pearl need Zog's help to catch a stink beetle for an urgent cure. Little do they know, Zog has become a taxi for the gnomes.

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: Elvis has forgotten his trainers and has to wear a pair with laces, but he can’t tie them without his gran’s help. He needs to quickly learn to tie them himself if he wants to get a PB.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi, Ruby and Finn struggle to score in basketball, so Rafi wishes for a magic ball. At first, it’s fun, as every shot goes in - even trick throws. But the constant winning becomes boring, and the ball bounces endlessly into the hoop by itself. The trio try to contain it, but it escapes again and again. Finally, they return to playing with the ordinary ball, and Finn sinks a real shot, proving true victory is earned.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: After playing with her toy dinosaurs in Gran Gran's garden, JoJo decides she would love to see a real-life dinosaur! Gran Gran takes her to the museum to see the fossilised skeleton of a Tyrannosaurus rex, explaining that dinosaurs lived a very long time ago! However, it's more difficult to find the T. rex than she imagined, despite it's size. JoJo and Gran Gran get lost through time as they explore the large museum, and it's only when Ezra the tour guide gives them guidance that JoJo and Gran Gran find the amazing artefact!

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. A search for shade on a hot day leads Sarah and Duck to discover a fascinating tower in the park.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Small has invited the Iron Chicken to a picnic. But the Iron Chicken is late, and when Small looks through his telescope, he can see why. The Iron Chicken is trapped by a load of junk metal which has got caught in orbit around her nest. Major comes up with a clever solution to free the nest of the orbiting metal, but in doing so it seems he may have inadvertently lost the Iron Chicken.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa show Gramma Leeba a photo of themselves and match the pose. On the way to the Play Tree, they spot shapes in the clouds. They choose a picture book to play with and match the shapes to each other and all their friends. The game is easy for MeMo, but BaBa needs a little more help. MeMo kindly helps BaBa to play the game until it’s time for BeddyByes.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: The Tombliboos are riding in the Pinky Ponk, enjoying their Pinky Ponk iuice. Each of them makes a different funny noise when they sip their juice. Despite a request from the narrator to drink their Pinky Ponk juice gently and quietly, the game continues until everyone in the garden can hear the funny noise coming from the Pinky Ponk.

programme.desc: Everybody's welcome to join Ewan McGregor for a Bedtime Story about a caring little mouse, who dreams of building a safe and happy home, where everyone feels that they belong.
